from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        label2.next_to(sphere, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere), Write(label2))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "High-dimensional volume behaves in counter-intuitive ways.",
            "Volume concentrates near the equator as n increases.",
            "Total volume tends toward zero as n grows.",
            "Imagine an orange in 100-dimensional space.",
            "Almost all fruit hides in the outer layer."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Paradox of Volume and Surface Area", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup animation elements
        vol_formula = MathTex("V_n(R) = \\frac{\\pi^{n/2}}{\\Gamma(n/2 + 1)}R^n", color="#FF5733")
        graph = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.2], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = graph.plot(lambda x: 1 / (x + 1), color="#33FF57")
        paradox_label = Text("Volume Paradox", font_size=30, color="#3357FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.place_at_grid(vol_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(vol_formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.place_at_grid(graph, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(graph), Create(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(paradox_label, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(paradox_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We use orthogonal projections to visualize 4D objects.", "A 4D sphere slices through our 3D reality.", "It appears, grows, peaks, and then vanishes."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Un-visualizable", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements for animation
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        label = Text("Hypersphere", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        
        # Animation: sphere appears/grows
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "D3", scale_factor=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere), sphere.animate.scale(10))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        
        # Animation: flash label
        self.play(Flash(label.get_center(), color="#3357FF", line_length=0.2))
        
        # Animation: sphere shrinks/vanishes
        self.play(sphere.animate.scale(0.1), FadeOut(sphere))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "High-dimensional geometry aids modern machine learning.",
            "The curse of dimensionality makes data points sparse.",
            "Finding patterns becomes harder in higher dimensions."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Applications: Data Science and Beyond", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'High-Dim Space' (color #FF5733)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")
        high_dim_label = Text("High-Dim Space", font_size=24, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(high_dim_label, "B2")
        self.play(FadeIn(high_dim_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show cluster points (color #33FF57)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#33FF57", radius=0.05) for _ in range(20)])
        for p in points:
            p.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + np.random.uniform(-0.5, 0.5, 3))
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate 'Dimension Reduction' label (color #3357FF)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")
        dr_label = Text("Dimension Reduction", font_size=24, color="#3357FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dr_label, "E5")
        self.play(Write(dr_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unveiling High-Dimensional Spheres: The Geometry of N-Dimensions

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Building Dimensions
sections.content: Briefly establish the transition from 1D (line), to 2D (circle), and 3D (sphere) using the general algebraic form: x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = r².
sections.example: Visualize a 'Flatland' character realizing that adding a third coordinate (z) transforms a circle into a sphere.

sections.title: Defining the N-Sphere
sections.content: Introduce the n-sphere (Sⁿ) as the set of points at a constant distance 'r' from a center in (n+1)-dimensional space. Emphasize that the 'dimension' refers to the surface manifold.
sections.example: A 1-sphere is the perimeter of a circle; a 2-sphere is the shell of a 3D ball; a 3-sphere is the 'surface' of a 4D hypersphere.

sections.title: The Paradox of Volume and Surface Area
sections.content: Explain how the volume of a unit n-ball behaves counter-intuitively as n increases—specifically, how volume concentrates near the 'equator' and eventually tends to zero as n goes to infinity.
sections.example: Imagine an orange in 100-dimensional space: almost all its 'fruit' (volume) is concentrated in a thin layer just beneath the 'peel' (surface).

sections.title: Visualizing the Un-visualizable
sections.content: Use orthogonal projection techniques to demonstrate how a 4D hypersphere (a Tesseract-like containment) would look if sliced through our 3D reality.
sections.example: An animation of a 4D sphere passing through 3D space: it appears as a point, grows into a sphere, reaches maximum size, shrinks, and vanishes.

sections.title: Applications: Data Science and Beyond
sections.content: Connect high-dimensional geometry to modern AI, specifically how 'Curse of Dimensionality' impacts machine learning algorithms.
sections.example: A robot learning to walk in high-dimensional state space: explain that as dimensions increase, data points become 'sparse,' making it harder for the robot to find the 'correct' movement pattern.
